 BIGBANG craze hits My Dinh Stadium: Hotels fully booked, airfares skyrocket.
 Thanks to BIGBANG's concert at My Dinh Stadium (Hanoi), the market for airline tickets and hotels in Hanoi has seen price increases, resulting in a shortage of rooms and tickets.
 VietNamNet • 23/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The BIGBANG 2026-2027 World Tour (XX: Cosmos) by the popular boy band BIGBANG was initially planned to take them through 19 cities with 33 shows. According to YG Entertainment's announcement, the group had already held shows in Goyang (South Korea), Oakland and East Rutherford (USA), Paris (France), London (England), Taipei (Taiwan, China), and Singapore .
 The selection of Hanoi as an official destination for the group's global tour demonstrates the high regard the Vietnamese market is receiving, especially after the success of G-Dragon's show last year. 
 BIGBANG is considered the kings of K-Pop. Even before BIGBANG arrived in Hanoi, the frenzy to hunt for tickets and lightsticks had spread throughout the fan community. 
 Nearly 70,000 people were recorded waiting in line to buy tickets just minutes after the supplementary ticket sales opened on October 5, 2026. Thousands of fans flocked to merchandise stores, and the resale market was bustling ahead of the two nights of concerts at My Dinh Stadium. BIGBANG's appeal in Hanoi is transcending the music story, becoming a consumer phenomenon linked to memories and fandom culture.
 Leading up to BIGBANG's appearance at My Dinh National Stadium in Hanoi, fans spent weeks racing to secure their spots for the two nights of concerts on October 24th and 25th. From the frantic ticket hunts online to the long queues for lightsticks, the hype surrounding the South Korean group was palpable on multiple fronts.
 On social media, the resale market has become very active. After tickets sold out quickly upon official release, many accounts resold them at prices 500,000 to 1 million VND higher than the original price. Some popular ticket categories saw prices inflated by one and a half times, or even double, the original price.
 According to a survey by VietNamNet reporters, thanks to BIGBANG's concert at My Dinh Stadium (Hanoi), the market for airline tickets and hotels in Hanoi has seen price increases, leading to a shortage of rooms and tickets. Furthermore, many scammers have taken advantage of this situation to profit significantly from intermediary accounts, inflating ticket prices by tens of millions of VND. 
 Thousands of people flocked to the ticket exchange area (wristbands) at My Dinh Stadium. Notably, the race to get tickets isn't just about affordability. With limited tickets available, fans also have to consider seating options, accompanying benefits, and the risks of buying from others. The fear of missing the chance to see their idols after years of waiting can lead some fans to accept higher-than-expected prices.
 From the race to grab tickets to the long lines of people waiting to buy lightsticks. 
 In the culture of the K-Pop entertainment industry, merchandise and lightsticks are indispensable for the fan community, especially when attending concerts.
 You may also like On October 16th, hundreds of fans lined up at a merchandise store in a Hanoi shopping mall hoping to get their hands on the 20th anniversary edition lightstick and other official souvenirs. Images of the long lines of people waiting were shared on Threads and quickly attracted attention.
 However, the initial excitement turned into disappointment when lightsticks and keychains, two of the most sought-after items, were not yet available for direct purchase. Customers were instructed to pre-order, while delivery times were not clearly guaranteed. This sparked controversy regarding the organization of the sales process, especially since many people had spent hours waiting. 
 Images and item lists at merchandise retail locations. Nevertheless, purchasing power did not cool down. On October 17th, thousands of people continued to queue at merchandise stores from early morning. Some waited from 5 am, and some fans even flew from Ho Chi Minh City to Hanoi just to hunt for souvenirs.
 According to published information, the tour's merchandise catalog includes nearly 70 products. Lightsticks are priced at 1.7 million VND, crown keychains at 700,000 VND, and T-shirts range from 1.3 to 3.5 million VND. Some products are priced higher, depending on the type and design.
 At this price point, buying merchandise is no longer a small expense in addition to the ticket price. A fan wanting to own a lightstick, a Hanoi-themed shirt, and a few accessories might need to budget several million dong, not including travel, accommodation, and other unforeseen expenses during the concert trip.
 Nevertheless, many people are still willing to spend money. For them, a lightstick is not simply a device that emits light during a concert. Thousands of lightsticks appearing together in the audience create a distinctive image of K-Pop concert culture, helping fans feel a stronger connection with the artists and the community. 
 BIGBANG's official lightstick. Items bearing the unique mark of Hanoi also have souvenir value. After the concert ends, a shirt printed with the city's name or an accessory from the tour can still be kept as a personal memento. Therefore, what fans buy is not just a tangible product, but also a memory of meeting their idols, a moment they've waited for for years.
 BIGBANG and the legendary value of a bygone era of youth. 
 Debuting in 2006, BIGBANG is one of the iconic names of the second generation of K-pop, helping to bring the genre closer to international audiences through timeless hits like Haru Haru, Fantastic Baby , and Bang Bang Bang. 
 For many VIPs (the name given to BIGBANG's fan community), the group is closely associated with their early years of exposure to K-pop. After nearly two decades, seeing their idols perform live has a different meaning than simply following a rising star. It can be an opportunity to revisit a part of their memories, while also marking a journey of companionship with the group through various stages of their lives as fans.
 You may also like The timing factor is even more significant as the Hanoi concert is part of BIGBANG's 20th anniversary tour. Such milestones often create special demand for tickets, limited-edition merchandise, and products associated with each venue. For fans, owning an item bearing the name "Hanoi" means preserving the significance of a specific tour, rather than simply buying a product named after their idols. 
 My Dinh Stadium is ready. That's also why the excitement doesn't stop at the group of fans who have already bought tickets. Those who haven't managed to get tickets are still finding ways to participate in the atmosphere through merchandise, fandom activities, and discussions on social media. Meanwhile, images of fans lining up, sharing their shopping experiences, and updating product availability continue to keep the event prominently featured on online platforms.
 Social media serves both as a reflection of the concert's appeal and as a catalyst for its amplification. A picture of long lines of people waiting to buy lightsticks can spark curiosity in those who weren't initially interested; a post about inflated ticket prices fuels debates about the cost of attendance. From there, the story of BIGBANG expands beyond music, touching upon how young people spend money, express their interests, and engage with the community.
 BIGBANG's "Bang Bang Bang" music video has garnered nearly 900 million views on YouTube.
